Renal Cell Carcinoma: The patient has a history of endometrioid endometrial carcinoma and presents with abdominal and pelvic pain. The contrast-enhanced CT scan shows a right renal mass with areas of fat attenuation, which is suggestive of renal cell carcinoma. The presence of a fatty tumor thrombus in the right renal vein extending to the inferior vena cava further supports this diagnosis.
Angiomyolipoma: The CT scan shows a renal mass with areas of fat attenuation, which is consistent with an angiomyolipoma. However, the presence of a fatty tumor thrombus in the right renal vein is less typical for this diagnosis.
